{{Short description|Numerical algorithms based on integrable systems}}
{{primary source|date=April 2020}}
'''Integrable algorithms''' are numerical algorithms that rely on basic ideas from the mathematical theory of [[integrable systems]].<ref>{{cite conference | last=Nakamura | first=Y. | title=A new approach to numerical algorithms in terms of integrable systems | publisher=IEEE | isbn=0-7695-2150-9 |conference=International Conference on Informatics Research for Development of Knowledge Society Infrastructure|year=2004| page= | doi=10.1109/icks.2004.1313425 | pages=194–205}}</ref>

==Background==
The theory of integrable systems has advanced with the connection between [[numerical analysis]]. For example, the discovery of solitons came from the numerical experiments to the [[KdV equation]] by [[Norman Zabusky]] and [[Martin David Kruskal]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Zabusky | first1=N. J. | last2=Kruskal | first2=M. D. | title=Interaction of "Solitons" in a Collisionless Plasma and the Recurrence of Initial States | journal=Physical Review Letters | publisher=American Physical Society (APS) | volume=15 | issue=6 | date=1965-08-09 | issn=0031-9007 | doi=10.1103/physrevlett.15.240 | pages=240–243| bibcode=1965PhRvL..15..240Z |doi-access=free}}</ref> Today, various relations between numerical analysis and integrable systems have been found ([[Toda lattice]] and [[numerical linear algebra]],<ref>{{cite journal | last=Sogo | first=Kiyoshi | title=Toda Molecule Equation and Quotient-Difference Method | journal=Journal of the Physical Society of Japan | publisher=Physical Society of Japan | volume=62 | issue=4 | date=1993-04-15 | issn=0031-9015 | doi=10.1143/jpsj.62.1081 | pages=1081–1084| bibcode=1993JPSJ...62.1081S }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Iwasaki | first1=Masashi | last2=Nakamura | first2=Yoshimasa | title=Accurate computation of singular values in terms of shifted integrable schemes | journal=Japan Journal of Industrial and Applied Mathematics | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=23 | issue=3 | year=2006 | issn=0916-7005 | doi=10.1007/bf03167593 | pages=239–259| s2cid=121824363 | url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.jjiam/1197390799 | url-access=subscription }}</ref> discrete soliton equations and [[series acceleration]]<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Papageorgiou | first1=V. | last2=Grammaticos | first2=B. | last3=Ramani | first3=A. | title=Integrable lattices and convergence acceleration algorithms | journal=Physics Letters A | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=179 | issue=2 | year=1993 | issn=0375-9601 | doi=10.1016/0375-9601(93)90658-m | pages=111–115| bibcode=1993PhLA..179..111P }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Chang | first1=Xiang-Ke | last2=He | first2=Yi | last3=Hu | first3=Xing-Biao | last4=Li | first4=Shi-Hao | title=A new integrable convergence acceleration algorithm for computing Brezinski–Durbin–Redivo-Zaglia's sequence transformation via pfaffians | journal=Numerical Algorithms | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=78 | issue=1 | date=2017-07-01 | issn=1017-1398 | doi=10.1007/s11075-017-0368-z | pages=87–106| s2cid=4974630 }}</ref>), and studies to apply integrable systems to numerical computation are rapidly advancing.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Nakamura | first=Yoshimasa | title=Algorithms associated with arithmetic, geometric and harmonic means and integrable systems | journal=Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=131 | issue=1–2 | year=2001 | issn=0377-0427 | doi=10.1016/s0377-0427(00)00316-2 | pages=161–174| bibcode=2001JCoAM.131..161N | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Chu | first=Moody T. | title=Linear algebra algorithms as dynamical systems | journal=Acta Numerica | publisher=Cambridge University Press (CUP) | volume=17 | date=2008-04-25 | issn=0962-4929 | doi=10.1017/s0962492906340019 | pages=1–86| s2cid=8746366 }}</ref>
==Integrable difference schemes==
Generally, it is hard to accurately compute the solutions of nonlinear differential equations due to its non-linearity. In order to overcome this difficulty, R. Hirota has made discrete versions of integrable systems with the viewpoint of "Preserve mathematical structures of integrable systems in the discrete versions".<ref>{{cite journal | last=Hirota | first=Ryogo | title=Nonlinear Partial Difference Equations. I. A Difference Analogue of the Korteweg-de Vries Equation | journal=Journal of the Physical Society of Japan | publisher=Physical Society of Japan | volume=43 | issue=4 | date=1977-10-15 | issn=0031-9015 | doi=10.1143/jpsj.43.1424 | pages=1424–1433| bibcode=1977JPSJ...43.1424H }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Hirota | first=Ryogo | title=Nonlinear Partial Difference Equations. II. Discrete-Time Toda Equation | journal=Journal of the Physical Society of Japan | publisher=Physical Society of Japan | volume=43 | issue=6 | date=1977-12-15 | issn=0031-9015 | doi=10.1143/jpsj.43.2074 | pages=2074–2078| bibcode=1977JPSJ...43.2074H }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Hirota | first=Ryogo | title=Nonlinear Partial Difference Equations III; Discrete Sine-Gordon Equation | journal=Journal of the Physical Society of Japan | publisher=Physical Society of Japan | volume=43 | issue=6 | date=1977-12-15 | issn=0031-9015 | doi=10.1143/jpsj.43.2079 | pages=2079–2086| bibcode=1977JPSJ...43.2079H }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Hirota | first=Ryogo | title=Nonlinear Partial Difference Equations. IV. Bäcklund Transformation for the Discrete-Time Toda Equation | journal=Journal of the Physical Society of Japan | publisher=Physical Society of Japan | volume=45 | issue=1 | date=1978-07-15 | issn=0031-9015 | doi=10.1143/jpsj.45.321 | pages=321–332| bibcode=1978JPSJ...45..321H }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last=Hirota | first=Ryogo | title=Nonlinear Partial Difference Equations. V. Nonlinear Equations Reducible to Linear Equations | journal=Journal of the Physical Society of Japan | publisher=Physical Society of Japan | volume=46 | issue=1 | date=1979-01-15 | issn=0031-9015 | doi=10.1143/jpsj.46.312 | pages=312–319| bibcode=1979JPSJ...46..312H }}</ref>

At the same time, [[Mark J. Ablowitz]] and others have not only made discrete soliton equations with discrete [[Lax pair]] but also compared numerical results between integrable difference schemes and ordinary methods.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Ablowitz | first1=M. J. | last2=Ladik | first2=J. F. | title=Nonlinear differential−difference equations | journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=16 | issue=3 | year=1975 | issn=0022-2488 | doi=10.1063/1.522558 | pages=598–603| bibcode=1975JMP....16..598A }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Ablowitz | first1=M. J. | last2=Ladik | first2=J. F. | title=Nonlinear differential–difference equations and Fourier analysis | journal=Journal of Mathematical Physics | publisher=AIP Publishing | volume=17 | issue=6 | year=1976 | issn=0022-2488 | doi=10.1063/1.523009 | pages=1011–1018| bibcode=1976JMP....17.1011A }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Ablowitz | first1=M. J. | last2=Ladik | first2=J. F. | title=A Nonlinear Difference Scheme and Inverse Scattering | journal=Studies in Applied Mathematics | publisher=Wiley | volume=55 | issue=3 | year=1976 | issn=0022-2526 | doi=10.1002/sapm1976553213 | pages=213–229}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Ablowitz | first1=M. J. | last2=Ladik | first2=J. F. | title=On the Solution of a Class of Nonlinear Partial Difference Equations | journal=Studies in Applied Mathematics | publisher=Wiley | volume=57 | issue=1 | year=1977 | issn=0022-2526 | doi=10.1002/sapm19775711 | pages=1–12}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Ablowitz | first1=Mark J. | last2=Segur | first2=Harvey | title=Solitons and the Inverse Scattering Transform | publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] | year=1981 | isbn=978-0-89871-174-5 | doi=10.1137/1.9781611970883 |location=Philadelphia}}</ref> As a result of their experiments, they have found that the accuracy can be improved with integrable difference schemes at some cases.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Taha | first1=Thiab R | last2=Ablowitz | first2=Mark J | title=Analytical and numerical aspects of certain nonlinear evolution equations. Analytical | journal=Journal of Computational Physics | publisher=Elsevier BV | volume=55 | issue=2 | year=1984 | issn=0021-9991 | doi=10.1016/0021-9991(84)90002-0 | pages=192–202| bibcode=1984JCoPh..55..192T }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Taha | first1=Thiab R | last2=Ablowitz | first2=Mark I | title=Analytical and numerical aspects of certain nonlinear evolution equations.
